Set up
Eden (Switch)
In Eden\'s controller settings, turn on motion and the UDP controller, with the address above as the server.
Then point each player\'s buttons, sticks and motion at the UDP controller. A player holding two Joy-Cons has two motion inputs — the second reads the other hand.
Create a file named DSUClient.ini inside Dolphin\'s user folder at Android/data/org.dolphinemu.dolphinemu/files/Config/, with exactly this content:
[Server]\nEnabled = True\nEntries = Joycon2:127.0.0.1:26760;
Then restart Dolphin. Under Wii Remote 1 → Emulated, a DSUClient device appears in the device dropdown.
Under Motion Input, map all Accelerometer and Gyroscope entries name-to-name, and map Recenter (gyro pointing drifts — press it in-game to summon the pointer).
Having trouble mapping buttons?

Press-a-button detection in Android emulators only sees Android input devices, so it never detects DSU inputs. Map them manually instead — pick from the DSU device\'s input list or type them in the expression field.
DSU buttons use DS4 names:
SL, SR and C have no DSU equivalent and aren\'t streamed.
A player holding two Joy-Cons streams both sets of buttons, but each hand needs a slot of its own to stream motion.
If the Virtual Gamepad is also on, detection grabs your press from it instead — turn it off while mapping DSU inputs.
